ranking_caption: Axis ranks prioritise interpretation of the available case evidence. Therapeutic ranks are provisional discussion orders based on relevant human evidence, mechanism and uncertainty; they are not response probabilities, gene-expression scores or proven comparative efficacy. Access limits remain alongside every option. Some agents appear under more than one connected mechanism.

axes.axis: Poor immune recruitment and an immune-poor state
axes.meaning: Too few useful immune cells may be attracted into the lesion.
axes.evidence: Low CXCR3 ligands across both research RNA samples and low BostonGene CXCL10; low CD3/NKG7 and non-inflamed portrait.
axes.uncertainty: Chemokine shortage is a credible phenotype, but could reflect too few activated cells rather than an intrinsic recruitment defect.
axes.inference: Moderate archival support; current lesion and direction of causality unresolved.
therapeutics: 1. Vactosertib + pembrolizumab or INCA33890: possible recruitment/entry effects
2. CXCL12/CXCR4 approaches: NOX-A12 + pembrolizumab or plerixafor-based studies
3. Personalised vaccine with optional systemic N-803: indirect recruitment support
axes.ranking_rationale: There is no validated recruitment-restoring treatment for this case. Vactosertib has direct human CRC activity; CXCL12 studies show tissue immune changes without objective responses. Vaccines/N-803 address priming and expansion more directly than recruitment.
axes.access_and_limits: Vactosertib’s trial excluded prior checkpoint treatment; post-BOT/BAL recruitment rescue is unproved. NOX-A12’s 20-patient mixed-cancer trial had no RECIST responses despite tissue changes. Neither vaccine nor N-803 reliably repairs chemokine gradients, collagen barriers or antigen display.

axes.meaning: Fibroblast signals and matrix may restrain immune entry or activity.
axes.evidence: Resection matrix RNA and selective B7 CAF proteins; CXCL12, THBS2 and ITGA5 leads.
axes.uncertainty: Caris counterevidence, muscle/repair admixture and near-median CTHRC1/LRRC15 RNA weaken a uniform suppressive-CAF diagnosis.
axes.inference: Strong resection stromal phenotype; actual physical exclusion unmeasured.
therapeutics: 1. Vactosertib + pembrolizumab and INCA33890: same discussion tier
2. CXCL12/CXCR4-directed approaches, including NOX-A12
3. Setanaxib or FAP-targeting radioligand/ADC strategies: distinct approaches with limited CRC evidence
4. Earlier or deprioritised approaches: PLN101095, NC410, and preclinical CTHRC1/integrin/LOX strategies
axes.ranking_rationale: Direct human CRC evidence puts vactosertib and INCA33890 ahead of less mature approaches. No head-to-head superiority is established, and high stromal or TGF-beta expression does not predict benefit. FAP-directed cytotoxicity is distinct from reversing immune exclusion.
axes.access_and_limits: Vactosertib/pembrolizumab produced 13/103 CRC responses and median PFS 1.2 months; most participants did not respond. No baseline TGF-beta/CAF predictor was validated. INCA33890’s more inflamed baseline profiles had better outcomes, while TGF-beta RNA was not associated. Setanaxib missed its primary endpoint in head-and-neck cancer; it has no established CRC efficacy. NC410 was terminated, and PLN101095/CTHRC1 approaches lack established CRC benefit. FAP access/uptake requirements remain agent-specific.

axes.meaning: Extracellular nucleotide processing may suppress immunity and innate danger signals.
axes.evidence: CD39/CD73/ENPP1 detection, with downstream innate-signalling components.
axes.uncertainty: No extracellular flux or current compartment measurements; CD39 can also mark useful T cells.
axes.inference: Coherent candidate, not demonstrated dependence or clinical eligibility biomarker.
therapeutics: 1. Etrumadenant-containing immunotherapy/chemotherapy regimen
2. RBS2418: ENPP1 inhibitor
3. Vizenpistat + botensilimab/balstilimab
4. Anti-CD73 agents such as oleclumab, or selective CD39 agents
axes.ranking_rationale: Etrumadenant leads on randomized whole-regimen CRC evidence, despite paused development. RBS2418 is a concrete ENPP1 trial lead with preliminary uncontrolled evidence. Negative CD73 trial findings outweigh target detection alone.
axes.access_and_limits: ARC-9 cannot isolate etrumadenant from its other active drugs; development is paused. RBS2418’s central trial biomarker is not interchangeable with separate archival bulk ENPP1 protein and cGAS RNA. Vizenpistat’s trial excludes prior PD-1/PD-L1 or CTLA4 therapy. COLUMBIA-1 was negative. Eligibility and supply are unconfirmed.

axes.meaning: Tumour antigen display or interferon responses may be insufficient for recognition.
axes.evidence: Low resection antigen-display RNA, APC/PTEN changes and PTPN proteins.
axes.uncertainty: Caris assay-matched results and retained bulk proteins oppose universal fixed loss.
axes.inference: A reversible or compositional explanation remains at least as plausible as an irreversible defect.
therapeutics: 1. AC484 (ABBV-CLS-484), with or without PD-1 blockade
2. APC11/TAT-APC11: preclinical APC-derived peptide
3. Selected epigenetic priming strategies: mixed human CRC evidence
4. NRF2/NBR1 or PTPN12 approaches: preclinical research only
axes.ranking_rationale: Human development and preclinical CRC evidence support discussing AC484 first. APC11 has a specific APC-related mechanism but remains preclinical; its position does not imply stronger human efficacy than epigenetic combinations, whose CRC results are mixed. No expression level or mutation selects a responder.
axes.access_and_limits: AC484 has early human renal-cancer evidence, not established CRC efficacy; Calico’s no-expanded-access policy conflicts with an older registry listing. APC11/TAT-APC11 requires clinical development and is not interchangeable with AC484. Commercial peptide synthesis does not establish suitability for human administration.

axes.axis: Myeloid suppression and clearance of dying cells
axes.meaning: Macrophages and clearance of dying cells may contribute to suppression.
axes.evidence: AXL/MERTK/GAS6/CSF1 and macrophage markers; SPP1 protein.
axes.uncertainty: No proven SPP1-dominant suppressive niche; resident cells and cell mixture confound.
axes.inference: Plausible contributor, intertwined with recruitment/stroma rather than independent confirmation.
therapeutics: 1. Zanzalintinib + atezolizumab
2. Selective AXL/MERTK or CSF1R/CCR2-directed agents; CXCR2 evidence is weak
3. CD47/SIRPA approaches: substantial combination-specific safety limits
axes.ranking_rationale: Zanzalintinib has whole-regimen phase 3 CRC evidence, but this does not isolate AXL inhibition. Selective myeloid agents have generally weak CRC signals; CD47 combinations require especially careful attention to observed serious toxicity.
axes.access_and_limits: Zanzalintinib’s trial excluded prior PD-1/PD-L1 treatment. BA3011 is an AXL-directed ADC, not equivalent to signalling blockade. CSF1R/pembrolizumab and CXCR2/navarixin/pembrolizumab had few CRC responses. Evorpacept/cetuximab/pembrolizumab had two treatment-related fatal immune syndromes; that empirical triple is not supported.

axes.axis: Insufficient priming or effective immune-cell pool
axes.meaning: Too few cells may recognise the relevant tumour targets or remain active.
axes.evidence: Low TMB, peripheral lymphopenia and mixed T/NK/DC gene patterns.
axes.uncertainty: No native tumour-reactivity measurement; liver contained T/NK cells and IL15 RNA is not low.
axes.inference: Insufficient useful cells is possible; absence of all effectors or cytokine deficiency is not established.
therapeutics: 1. Personalised tumour-reactive TCR therapy
2. Personalised neoantigen vaccine as a priming component
3. Investigational systemic N-803 as an expansion/activation partner
4. Repeat botensilimab/balstilimab without a demonstrated new mechanism
axes.ranking_rationale: Tumour-reactive TCR therapy supplies selected cells and has early CRC responses, with major treatment and access burdens. Vaccines have human MSS CRC priming evidence and occasional responses. N-803 supports cell expansion but has weaker evidence for CRC tumour control; it is a potential partner, not an antigen-specific substitute.
axes.access_and_limits: TCR therapy requires suitable antigen/HLA recognition, manufacturing and fitness for intensive treatment. Personalised vaccine trials demonstrate priming more consistently than tumour response. QuICC had 0/12 responses with shared-antigen vaccine/N-803/bintrafusp and 1/20 after adding targeted IL-12; the responder was checkpoint-naive. Systemic N-803 is investigational and distinct from bladder-only intravesical ANKTIVA. Repeat BOT/BAL benefit after prior exposure is unestablished.

axes.meaning: The prostaglandin PGE2 may inhibit immune-cell activity.
axes.uncertainty: COX2/EP4 proteins unassigned; PGE2 unmeasured and CRC trials weak.
axes.inference: Secondary hypothesis with no predictive biomarker here.
therapeutics: 1. ONO-4578 + nivolumab in an appropriate study
2. Other selective EP4 agents such as E7046
3. COX2 inhibition: no established immune-rescue role in this case
axes.ranking_rationale: The ordering follows the limited human CRC signal rather than the high PTGS2 RNA value. All remain low-confidence immune strategies.
axes.access_and_limits: ONO-4578/nivolumab had 2/51 CRC responses; the current first-line trial excludes prior checkpoint treatment. E7046 monotherapy had no objective responses in 30 patients. Prior ulcer bleeding weighs against empirical aspirin or celecoxib.

axes.meaning: Vessels, oxygen supply or metabolism may limit immune access and function.
axes.evidence: Some endothelial/metabolic markers and historical liver CA9.
axes.uncertainty: Caris VEGFA 6th and BostonGene 15th; no perfusion/oxygen data, rank-sensitive signatures.
axes.inference: A generic plausible mechanism, weakly selected by this case.
therapeutics: 1. An evidence-based bevacizumab-containing standard CRC regimen where indicated
2. Zanzalintinib + atezolizumab as an immune/vascular strategy
3. Lenvatinib + pembrolizumab or other unsupported vascular/checkpoint combinations
axes.ranking_rationale: Established CRC efficacy supports a standard bevacizumab regimen when clinically appropriate, independently of this resistance hypothesis. Experimental vascular/checkpoint combinations have more uncertain benefit and greater extrapolation after prior checkpoint therapy.
axes.access_and_limits: This does not rank all standard CRC treatments. Zanzalintinib’s trial excluded prior checkpoint exposure; LEAP-017 missed its primary overall-survival endpoint. Bevacizumab should not simply be added to panitumumab/cetuximab. Prior bleeding and radiotherapy remain relevant to clinical review.

axes.meaning: Additional receptor–ligand interactions may inhibit T or NK cells.
axes.evidence: HLA-E and other checkpoint ligands; historical liver receptor RNA.
axes.uncertainty: HLA-G protein assignment unconfirmed; receptor engagement and dominance unknown.
axes.inference: No evidence selects a particular alternative checkpoint as the main obstacle.
therapeutics: 1. TTX080 + cetuximab
2. Monalizumab + durvalumab
3. TIGIT, galectin or TIM3-directed trial agents
axes.ranking_rationale: Small human CRC studies support discussion, but neither target RNA nor protein detection supplies a validated selection rule. All remain low absolute priority.
axes.access_and_limits: TTX080 evidence is small and uncontrolled, with cetuximab contribution unresolved and an active-not-recruiting trial. The case’s HLA-G-labelled peptide is shared with other HLA proteins. Monalizumab/durvalumab had 3/39 responses in evaluable MSS CRC; receptor expression alone does not predict benefit.
